styles.name: sieve-eratosthenes
styles.description: Sieve of Eratosthenes: integers cross composites, primes survive as lit dots

styles.name: ulam-spiral
styles.description: Ulam spiral: integers wind outward from the centre in a rectangular spiral that tiles the bar, only primes lit — the tell-tale diagonal streaks appear as progress unwinds it, with a blinking head marking the newest integer

styles.name: prime-counting
styles.description: π(x) prime-counting function: a rising step curve filling as primes accumulate

styles.name: collatz
styles.description: Collatz (3n+1): seeds swept left→right, trajectory height is stopping sequence depth

styles.name: fibonacci-spiral
styles.description: Fibonacci spiral: squares of side 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 tile a 13×8 rectangle and a quarter arc sweeps through each; three tilings build square by square as progress rises, and a bead rides the finished spirals with time

styles.name: pascal-mod
styles.description: Pascal's triangle mod p laid on its side: row n runs along the bar, the middle binomials C(n, k) stack up the height, and every entry not divisible by p is lit — nested triangular holes open up as progress adds rows; p cycles 2, 3, 5 with time

styles.name: totient-histogram
styles.description: Euler totient φ(n): columns show φ(n)/n — primes spike to the top, composites sag

styles.name: stern-brocot
styles.description: Stern–Brocot tree: 1/1 at the top, each node's children the mediants with its neighbours (1/2, 2/1, 1/3, 2/3, 3/2, 3/1…), in sorted order — the binary tree of all positive rationals grows level by level with progress while a walker blinks down the path that converges on the golden ratio

styles.name: continued-fraction-phi
styles.description: Convergents of φ = [1;1,1,…] — 1/1, 2/1, 3/2, 5/3, 8/5… — plotted left to right as a zig-zag that alternates above and below the dotted golden-ratio line and closes in on it (error on a log scale); progress adds convergents, a marker rides the newest

styles.name: modular-circle
styles.description: Times-table chord diagrams: points round a circle, chord k→m·k mod N — a row of circles for m = 2, 3, 4, … strung chord by chord as progress advances, each chord envelope (cardioid, nephroid, three-cusp epicycloid…) traced solid, the figures turning slowly with time

styles.name: recaman
styles.description: Recamán's sequence 0, 1, 3, 6, 2, 7, 13, 20, 12, 21, 11, … drawn the classic way: each jump a half-arc over the number line, alternating above and below, nesting into rainbows as progress adds terms; a bead runs along the newest arc

styles.name: digital-root-vortex
styles.description: Vortex math: digital-root cycles 1–9 drawn as chords on a circle, revealing mod-9 symmetry
